listing.name: Dune II (Dune Dynasty)
listing.summary: Set up Dune Dynasty, an enhanced OpenDUNE-derived engine, with your own European Dune II v1.07 data. Windows, Linux and macOS releases are offered; select the package for your CPU rather than relying on build badges. The project builds Windows x86, x86-64 and ARM64, and macOS x86-64 and ARM64 versions. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

steps.title: Finish Dune Dynasty setup before attaching it
steps.instruction: Use a permitted complete Windows Dune Dynasty copy with your own European Dune II 1.07 PAK files, following upstream’s FILELIST.TXT. Keep those data files in the prepared data directory or the actual personal Dune Dynasty/data directory used by the copy. Missing original data makes normal startup fail; attaching the engine alone does not prepare it. Optional music, soundfonts and enhancements have separate requirements and rights.

steps.title: Keep the existing portable or personal profile choice
steps.instruction: Select native dunedynasty.exe and its actual prepared working directory. Keep dunedynasty.cfg: an existing executable-side config selects portable state; otherwise Windows normally uses the current account’s roaming AppData/Dune Dynasty profile. Do not create an executable-side config merely to register the game. Preserve that whole actual profile, its save directory, configuration, original data, custom campaigns/music and the old creating runtime before replacement. Original-format save reading is not a promise that every newer save works in an older engine.

steps.title: Check the working copy before registration
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools, then start and quit the copy you intend to add. Keep its game executable, working folder and supported launch arguments. Review those details in Portcove and agree to launch them, then choose Play separately. Adding a copy does not confirm its game files or save compatibility.

steps.title: Keep updates and removal under the existing owner
steps.instruction: Close every running copy of the game before changing files. Keep the working game version and every data and profile folder recoverable. Update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable in Portcove before choosing Play. You manage setup, updates, file changes, data migration and recovery. Portcove monitors the process you selected; it does not prevent other copies from running or restrict the game’s file access. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion.

warnings: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant rights to original game assets, music, mods or bundled components.
Before updating the game, keep a copy of its working files and every location containing saved data. Choosing a different executable does not give it a separate profile.
